上海

Shanghai

Where tradition meets tomorrow

Shanghai is a city of layers — Art Deco heritage buildings hiding Michelin-worthy dumpling shops, rooftop cocktail bars above 1930s slaughterhouses, and water towns that feel frozen in the Ming dynasty. Beyond the Bund clichés lies a city that rewards the curious.

Shanghai Natural History Museum (上海自然博物馆)

Housed in a stunning building shaped like a nautilus shell, designed by an international architecture firm. World-class exhibits on dinosaurs, evolution, and earth sciences. The atrium alone is breathtaking — a vast sunlit space with hanging whale skeletons and towering dinosaur fossils. TripAdvisor's top-rated Shanghai museum.

510 Beijing West Road, Jing'an District Line 13 Natural History Museum Station
Open in AMap Book Tickets →
¥30 (adults) / ¥15 (students) 3 photos
Click to collapse

Shanghai Astronomy Museum (上海天文馆)

The world's largest planetarium and astronomy museum. A futuristic, architecturally stunning building with zero straight lines — designed to evoke orbits and celestial mechanics. Immersive exhibits, a massive domed theater, and interactive space exploration displays. Consistently rated as one of the most mind-blowing museums in Asia. Located in the Lingang area.

3800 Wanhangdu Road (Weekend Express) / Lingang area, Pudong Line 16 Dishui Lake Station
Open in AMap Book Tickets →
¥25 5 photos
Click to collapse

Propaganda Poster Art Centre (宣传画艺术中心)

A truly unique and quirky private museum hidden on the basement floor of a residential building. Houses one of the world's largest collections of original Chinese propaganda posters from the 1950s-1980s. Fascinating window into China's political and social history. Run by a passionate collector. Very off-the-beaten-path — you'd never find it without knowing about it.

726 Yanan Road West (Bldg 2B, Basement) Line 10/11 Jiaotong University Station
Open in AMap
Free 3 photos
Click to collapse

Shanghai Museum (People's Square) (上海博物馆)

One of China's four great museums, housing over 1.2 million pieces of ancient Chinese art. World-renowned for its bronze, ceramics, calligraphy, and jade collections. The building itself is inspired by an ancient bronze vessel. Free entry with online reservation. Plan 2-3 hours minimum.

201 Renmin Avenue, Huangpu District Line 1/2/8 People's Square Station
Open in AMap

Jing'an Temple (静安寺)

One of Shanghai's most famous ancient Buddhist temples, dating back 1,800 years. Stunning golden rooftops visible from the street, surrounded by modern skyscrapers. The contrast between ancient temple and futuristic city is uniquely Shanghai. Three halls with exquisite Buddha statues and a peaceful central courtyard.

北京

Beijing

Emperors, alleyways, and everything after

Beijing isn't just the Forbidden City and Great Wall. It's underground techno clubs in former bomb shelters, 400-year-old courtyard villages you can stay in, the world's best Peking duck in holes-in-the-wall, and temples older than most countries. The real Beijing hides behind the tourist facade.

Capital Museum (首都博物馆)

Beijing's premier city museum showcasing 3,000 years of the capital's history. World-class exhibits of ancient bronzes, calligraphy, porcelain, jade, and traditional Beijing folk art. The stunning modern building itself is an architectural landmark. Free entry with passport reservation.

16 Fuxingmen Outer Street, Xicheng District Line 1 Muxidi Station
Open in AMap Book Tickets →
Free 6 photos
Click to collapse

National Museum of China (国家博物馆)

The second most visited museum in the world, located on Tiananmen Square. Covers the entire sweep of Chinese civilization from prehistory to modern era. Over 1.4 million artifacts including the famous Simuwu Ding bronze vessel. Plan at least half a day — this museum is massive.

16 East Chang'an Street, Dongcheng District Line 1 Tiananmen East Station
Open in AMap Book Tickets →
¥20 4 photos
Click to collapse

Poly Art Museum (保利艺术博物馆)

Hidden gem on the 9th floor of the Poly Group building. Houses an extraordinary collection of ancient Chinese bronzes and Buddhist stone sculptures, many repatriated from overseas auctions. Compact, uncrowded, and surprisingly affordable. A true connoisseur's museum.

14 Dongzhimen South Main Street, Dongcheng District Line 2 Dongzhimen Station
Open in AMap Book Tickets →
Free 3 photos
Click to collapse

Beijing Urban Planning Exhibition Hall (北京规划展览馆)

A fascinating look at Beijing's past, present, and future urban development. The highlight is a massive scale model of the entire city showing every building and street. Multi-media exhibits on Beijing's history of city planning from imperial grid to modern mega-city. A Quora favorite as the most underrated museum in Beijing.

20 Qianmendong Main Street, Dongcheng District Line 2 Qianmen Station

Temple of Confucius & Guozijian Museum (孔庙和国子监博物馆)

Beijing's oldest and largest Confucian temple, alongside the Imperial College (Guozijian) where scholars studied for 700+ years. Ancient cypress trees, stone steles, and tranquil courtyards. Far less crowded than other Beijing temples. One of the most atmospheric spots in the city.

Summer Palace (颐和园)

China's largest and most well-preserved imperial garden. UNESCO World Heritage site with the iconic Long Corridor, Marble Boat, and Kunming Lake. Stunning in every season. A must-visit for anyone coming to Beijing — the emperor's playground is breathtaking.

19 Xinjian Gongmen Road, Haidian District Line 4 Beigongmen Station
Open in AMap Book Tickets →
¥20 (Bell) / ¥20 (Drum) / ¥30 (combo) 3 photos

Bell Tower & Drum Tower (钟鼓楼)

Iconic twin towers that once kept time for the entire city. Climb the Drum Tower for one of the best panoramic views of the hutong rooftops. Drum performances every hour. The area between them is a vibrant public square with local life, street performers, and incredible photo opportunities.

Zhonglouwan, Dongcheng District Line 2/8 Gulou Dajie Station
Open in AMap
¥10 (entrance) / ¥25 (full ticket) 3 photos
Click to collapse

Yuanmingyuan Ruins Park (圆明园遗址公园)

The Old Summer Palace, destroyed by British and French troops in 1860. hauntingly beautiful ruins of European-style palaces surrounded by peaceful lakes and gardens. A powerful historical site that tells the story of imperial China's downfall. The restored sections are also lovely for walking.

28 Qinghua West Road, Haidian District Line 4 Yuanmingyuan Park Station

深圳

Shenzhen

China's Silicon Coast

Shenzhen gets dismissed as a factory city. Wrong. It has the country's best contemporary art scene, pristine beaches the locals don't want tourists to know about, Hakka villages older than Hong Kong, and a creative energy that makes Brooklyn look sleepy. China's youngest major city is its most surprising.

Guangzhou

Cantonese soul, no filter

Guangzhou is where Chinese food was invented (basically). It's also where you'll find colonial-era islands with banyan tree canopies, 2,000-year-old tombs of kings, anarchist book cafes, and the kind of 3am street food scenes that make you question every Cantonese restaurant you've ever eaten at back home.

Chen Clan Ancestral Hall (陈家祠)

The crown jewel of Cantonese architecture. Built in 1894 by the Chen clan, this ancestral hall features some of the finest decorative art in all of China — intricate wood carvings, stone carvings, pottery sculptures, iron castings, and painted clay. The craftsmanship is absolutely jaw-dropping. Now houses the Guangdong Folk Art Museum.

20 Zhongshan 7th Road, Liwan District Line 1/8 Chen Clan Academy Station
Open in AMap
6 photos
Click to collapse

Temple of the Six Banyan Trees (六榕寺)

One of Guangzhou's oldest and most important Buddhist temples, founded in 537 AD. The iconic Flowery Pagoda rises beautifully above the temple complex. Inside, massive bronze Buddha statues and serene meditation halls. A peaceful escape in the heart of the city with over 1,500 years of history.

87 Liurong Road, Yuexiu District Line 1 Ximenkou Station
Open in AMap
¥5 3 photos
Click to collapse

Guangxiao Temple (光孝寺)

One of the oldest Buddhist temples in Guangzhou, with a history stretching back over 1,700 years. Known as the place where the eminent monk Huineng (the 6th Chan Patriarch) had his head shaved. Features ancient pagodas, iron towers, and a giant banyan tree. Far less touristy than Six Banyan Trees — a genuine local spiritual site.

109 Guangxiao Road, Yuexiu District Line 1 Ximenkou Station
Open in AMap
Free 3 photos
Click to collapse

Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall (中山纪念堂)

A grand octagonal building built in 1931 in honor of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, the founding father of modern China. Stunning architecture with no pillars obstructing the interior — an engineering marvel of its era. Beautiful surrounding park. Free to view from outside; concerts and events inside.

259 Dongfeng Middle 2nd Road, Yuexiu District Line 2 Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall Station
Open in AMap
